question: Your team builds the customer support agent with the Claude Agent SDK, and every developer needs the backend MCP server that provides get_customer, lookup_order, process_refund and escalate_to_human. One developer, Priya, also wants to try an experimental MCP server that drafts refund-policy summaries, and she is unsure whether it will work. Teammates who clone the repository should get the backend server automatically, but they should never see Priya's trial server. How should the two servers be configured?

options.text: Define the backend server in the project's committed .mcp.json, and define Priya's experimental server in her user-level ~/.claude.json.
options.reason: Project-level .mcp.json is the scope for shared team tooling, so cloning delivers it. User-level ~/.claude.json is the scope for personal or experimental servers, so teammates never see the trial server.

options.text: Define the backend server in each developer's user-level ~/.claude.json, and define Priya's experimental server in the project's committed .mcp.json.
options.reason: This reverses the two scopes. The shared backend server would not come with the repository, and Priya's experimental server would be pushed to every teammate through the committed .mcp.json.

options.text: Define both servers in each developer's user-level ~/.claude.json, and share the backend server's settings with new teammates through a wiki page.
options.reason: User-level ~/.claude.json is for personal servers and does not travel with the repository. New teammates would not get the shared backend server automatically, so it belongs in the project-level .mcp.json.

options.text: Define both servers in the project's committed .mcp.json, and ask teammates to ignore the experimental server's tools during their work.
options.reason: Any server in the committed .mcp.json is shared with the whole team. The experimental server would reach every teammate, which the requirement forbids, so it belongs in Priya's user-level ~/.claude.json.
